newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian stocks mixed, Pliva up in dull trade.
newsitem.headline: Croatian stocks mixed, Pliva up in dull trade.

text.p: Croatian stocks were stable to lower on shrinking volume on Thursday, with blue chip drugs firm Pliva the only gainer, and brokers said dull trading would continue throughout the festive season.
"It will be dull, which is typical of December. There is nothing to spur on the prices," a trader at Metroholding brokerage told Reuters.
He said Pliva, Thursday's sole gainer, went even further up on the Zagreb bourse than it did in London.
It rose 300 kuna to 13,300 on volume of 269 shares.
Zagrebacka Banka, the other fully listed stock, was the most active. It held its ground at 980 kuna, on volume of 2,000 units sold.
The trader said only the two blue chips could count on active trading in December, while other stocks would have "low trading and prices, as there are few big investors".
Apart from Pliva, two issues were flat and two down.
Volume was halved to 3,313 shares, turnover was also down to 5.8 million kuna.
The biggest decliner was confectioner Kras, which lost 10 kuna to 400, selling 357 shares. The other loser was food processor Podravka, down 2 kuna to 205, with 296 shares sold.
The second tranche of public debt refinancing bonds traded flat at 7.10 above par on turnover of 0.8 million kuna.
